title: Pietersen named specialist mentor for England white-ball teams ahead of 2027 World Cup
dek: Former England captain Kevin Pietersen, 46, has been appointed as specialist mentor to the white-ball teams ahead of the 2027 ICC Men's Cricket World Cup. It is his first involvement with the senior England side since 2014. He will start with matches against Sri Lanka beginning September 15.
author: The GoCheckMySports Desk
key_fact: Pietersen, sacked from England in 2014, returns as specialist mentor to Brendon McCullum's white-ball squad for the 2027 World Cup in Southern Africa.
bottom_line: Pietersen's debut as England mentor arrives on September 15 against Sri Lanka; the first-hand assessment of his dynamic with McCullum and the team's alignment on white-ball strategy will surface in that three-match series and the subsequent winter tours.
body: Kevin Pietersen, 46, has been appointed as specialist mentor to England's white-ball teams in preparation for the 2027 ICC Men's Cricket World Cup, according to announcements on September 7. The appointment marks his first involvement with the senior England side since his controversial departure in 2014 following the Ashes whitewash in Australia.

Pietersen will join the backroom staff of head coach Brendon McCullum and work alongside assistant coaches Marcus Trescothick and Jeetan Patel, with Sarah Taylor overseeing fielding and wicketkeeping and Tim Southee managing the fast bowlers. His role begins immediately with England's white-ball fixtures against Sri Lanka starting September 15 in Southampton and continues through to the 50-over World Cup in Southern Africa, per the Guardian.

McCullum said of the appointment, per the Guardian: "I've got immense respect for KP and what he's achieved in the game. He's had an amazing impact on English cricket, so for someone with his experience, knowledge and stature to want to play a role with this team is a fantastic result. I'm particularly excited for our batters to get the opportunity to work with him. KP has a unique understanding of what it takes to perform at the highest level, which will be hugely valuable to our players."

Pietersen's career record supports that assessment. Per BBC Sport, he scored nearly 4,500 ODI runs at an average of 41.32, bettered only by Joe Root, and holds the highest average of all English batters with more than 1,000 T20 runs. The BBC reports he was named player of the tournament when England won the T20 World Cup in 2010.

The ECB stated that Pietersen's South African upbringing will particularly benefit the one-day team as it prepares for next year's World Cup in South Africa, Zimbabwe and Namibia. Pietersen himself said, per the Guardian: "I am immensely proud to have been asked to help this team on their journey to win a World Cup in South Africa. Putting on the England uniform again for the first time since 2014 is a profound honour and a deeply special moment."

Pietersen's path to this role carried friction. Per BBC Sport, he was dropped during a 2012 Test series against South Africa for sending text messages to opposing players and was accused of being "divisive" in the dressing room. The BBC also reported Pietersen advocated early for England players to play in the Indian Premier League and other white-ball franchise leagues, a stance that often put him at odds with his employers. Since retiring from playing, he has worked as a commentator, content creator and mentor in the Indian Premier League for Delhi Capitals, and spoke publicly in 2025 about his coaching ambitions after England's 4-1 Ashes loss in Australia.
Pietersen will also be involved in this winter's tours to Australia and South Africa before rejoining the teams for the home series against Pakistan and New Zealand next summer.
